places.description: A compact family home on a busy residential street in a tropical coastal city, with small businesses and shared outdoor space nearby.
A mixed-day public school with ordinary classrooms, a science lab, a library room, sports grounds and student clubs whose availability varies with staffing.
A busy minibus and shared-taxi junction linking residential districts, markets, schools and the waterfront.
A major open market with food, fabric, electronics, household goods, repair services and many independent traders.
A community center used for tutoring, youth groups, public-health sessions, local meetings, performances and occasional skills workshops.

householdShape: Two caregivers, the subject and two cousins share a household; one cousin is older and one is younger, and their parent works in another city for long periods.
familyRelations: The cousins are treated as part of the daily household even though their parent remains involved from another city.
Several relatives live elsewhere in the same metropolitan area and are seen irregularly.
materialCircumstances: Household income is adequate for essentials but uneven across the year; school costs, transport, repairs and support for relatives require planning and tradeoffs.
mobilityPattern: Daily movement relies on walking, minibuses and shared taxis; occasional trips reach the waterfront, central business district and relatives in other parts of the city.
schoolingOrCommunityContext: School, market commerce, neighborhood religious and secular groups, community programs and extended family expose the subject to people with different ages, occupations and viewpoints.
culturalContext: The city combines coastal commerce, services, transport work, public institutions, multilingual households, religious communities, entertainment and civic life; routines are shaped by congestion, weather and changing prices without implying any required values.
intellectualEnvironment: School materials, local and international radio, library books, market knowledge, technical repair practice, public-health information, music and performance, religious/philosophical texts, family discussion and civic disagreement are available without a prescribed hierarchy.
